title: Torus and unipotent direct factors of a commutative group over a perfect field
statement:
Let $k$ be a perfect field [def-weil-field], meaning that either $\operatorname{char}k=0$, or $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and every element of $k$ is a $p$-th power. Let $G$ be a smooth geometrically connected commutative affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There are smooth geometrically connected closed $k$-subgroups $U,T\subseteq G$ [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] for which multiplication is an isomorphism of $k$-group schemes
$$U\times_kT\xrightarrow{\sim}G$$
[def-pc-fibre-product]. The group $T$ is a torus: after extension to an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] it is isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{m,\bar k}^s$ for an integer $s\geq0$, with $\mathbf G_m$ as in [def-sc-gm-ga]. The group $U$ admits a closed group embedding over $k$ into $\mathcal U_n$ for some $n\geq1$, where $\mathcal U_n(R)$ consists of upper triangular $n\times n$ matrices with diagonal entries $1$, under matrix multiplication, for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$. Both factors may be trivial. The torus $T$ is not asserted to be split over $k$.

source.place: Theorem 16.13(b) and its proof, printed p.328; Corollary 16.15 and the paragraph on smoothness and connectedness immediately before it, p.329; unitriangular realization by Theorem 14.5.

proof.text: Fix an algebraic closure $L=\bar k$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The extension $L/k$ is Galois: it is algebraic and normal because every polynomial splits in $L$, and it is separable as follows. For $a\in L$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis] to the finitely generated algebraic extension $k(a)/k$. Its transcendence basis must be empty, so $k(a)/k$ is separable. Apply [lem-sfb-commutative-diagonalizable-unipotent-product] to $G_L$ to obtain closed factors $V,D$ with $V\times_L D\simeq G_L$, with $V$ closed in an upper unitriangular group and $D\simeq\operatorname{Spec}L[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$. The quasi-inverse in [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], applied over $L$ with trivial Galois action, identifies this $D$ as a group of multiplicative type. No assertion of smoothness of the factors is needed at this point.

source.place: Theorem 16.13(b), proof: reduction to an algebraically closed field, printed p.328.

proof.text: This pair of subgroup schemes is unique. Indeed, let $V',D'$ be another such pair. The projection $G_L\to D$ restricts trivially to $V'$ by [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial], so $V'\subseteq V$ as subgroup schemes; reversing the pairs gives equality. The projection $G_L\to V$ restricts trivially to $D'$ by [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-to-unipotent-trivial], so $D'\subseteq D$, and reversal again gives equality. These factorizations hold on all algebra-valued points, not just on $L$-points.

source.place: Theorem 16.13(b), first paragraph of the proof, printed p.328.

proof.text: For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)$, the canonical semilinear action on $G_L$ takes $(V,D)$ to another pair of the same kind: twisting the unitriangular embedding preserves its equations with coefficients $0,1$, and twisting $L[M]$ gives $L[M]$ again. Twisting the product isomorphism gives a product isomorphism for the new pair. Uniqueness from step 2 gives $\sigma V=V$ and $\sigma D=D$. Thus their defining ideals are stable. By [lem-sfb-galois-descent-affine-subgroups], there are unique closed $k$-subgroups $U,T\subseteq G$ whose scalar extensions are $V,D$. The infinite Galois extension allowed by that node applies to $L/k$.

source.place: Theorem 16.13(b), Galois-descent sentence, p.328; Section 1.54(a)-(b), pp.21-22.

proof.text: Since $G$ is commutative, multiplication $m:U\times_kT\to G$ is a group-scheme homomorphism. Its extension to $L$ is the isomorphism of step 1. The field-extension morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat, surjective and quasi-compact by [lem-pc-field-extension-fpqc-cover]. Its base change $G_L\to G$ is a singleton fpqc covering by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. The map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], its base change $G_L\to G$ is affine and hence quasi-compact; the covering condition gives flatness and surjectivity. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-isomorphism] applies to $m$ over the target $G$, proving that $m$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse is a group homomorphism because $m$ is one.

source.place: Theorem 16.13(b), descent of the product isomorphism, p.328; affine fpqc detection made explicit.

proof.text: Both $U$ and $T$ are normal, since $G$ is commutative. Under the product isomorphism, $G/T\simeq U$ and $G/U\simeq T$: the projection to $U$ has kernel $T$, and every pair $(u,t)$ has the same $T$-coset as $(u,1)$, functorially for every algebra; the other identification is identical with the factors exchanged. These identifications hold already for the quotient presheaves and hence for their fppf sheafifications. The quotient assertion of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] now shows that both factors are smooth and geometrically connected, because $G$ is. It also ensures that the represented quotients used here have the stated group-scheme meanings.

source.place: Paragraph immediately before Corollary 16.14, printed p.329.

proof.text: The group $T$ is of multiplicative type: $T_L=D$ is of multiplicative type by step 1, and [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial] states that multiplicative type can be tested after field extension. By [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus], a smooth connected group of multiplicative type is a torus. Apply this to $T$, which is smooth and geometrically connected by step 5. This gives $T_L\simeq\mathbf G_{m,L}^s$ with $s\geq0$, without asserting such an isomorphism over $k$.

source.place: Corollary 16.15, first sentence of its proof, p.329; Theorems 12.8-12.9, pp.233-234.

proof.text: Choose a faithful closed representation $\rho:U\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$ with $m\geq1$ by [lem-sfb-affine-group-faithful-linear-representation]. Over $L$, identify $U_L$ with $V$. The embedding $i:V\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_{r,L}\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{r,L}$ from step 1 is faithful on all algebra points, and $(i(v)-I)^r=0$ for every $v\in V(L)$, since a strictly upper triangular $r\times r$ matrix has zero $r$-th power. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-representation-unipotent-point] with this $i$ and with $\rho_L$ as the other representation. Every $\rho_L(v)$ is therefore unipotent. Since $U$ is smooth by step 5, [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-unitriangular-embedding] gives a closed embedding $U\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_{n,k}$ over $k$ for some $n\geq1$. This supplies the required embedding over the original field, rather than just its algebraic closure.

source.place: Theorem 14.5(a)-(b), pp.281-282; Corollary 14.12, p.283; Corollary 16.15, p.329.

proof.text: The constructed $U,T$ are closed subgroups, and step 4 gives precisely multiplication $U\times_kT\simeq G$. Steps 5-7 give all the remaining clauses. No positive dimension was assumed: if either factor is trivial it remains smooth and geometrically connected; for the trivial unipotent factor take $n=1$, and for the trivial torus take $s=0$.

source.place: Corollary 16.15, p.329, including the zero-dimensional cases.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q138-58d834e11 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS: I read the item in full; the delivery makes no new nodes and changes neither the statement nor the stmt_deps. The proof follows Milne iAG2017 Thm 16.13(b) (p.328: uniqueness by 14.18 in both directions, k^a Galois over perfect k, descent), the p.329 paragraph (factors are quotients, hence smooth and connected) and Cor 16.15 (smooth connected multiplicative type is a torus). Step 1: k̄/k is Galois by the separating-basis Mathlib leaf; the algebraically closed product comes from commutative-diagonalizable-unipotent-product, which assumes no smoothness; D has multiplicative type by antiduality. Step 2: uniqueness from unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial and diagonalizable-to-unipotent-trivial; both hold on all algebra points and allow nonreduced and p-torsion groups. Step 3: σ-twists preserve U_n and L[M], since both are defined over the prime ring; galois-descent-affine-subgroups allows an infinite Galois extension. Step 4: G_L→G is flat, surjective and quasi-compact by the fpqc-cover, base-change and affine-permanence nodes, so fpqc-descend-isomorphism applies to m, and m_L is the step-1 isomorphism. Step 5: G/T ≅ U already as presheaves; the smooth and geometrically connected clauses of affine-normal-quotient-geometry then apply. Step 6: smooth connected multiplicative type gives a torus via largest-subtorus; the torus is not claimed to be split over k. Step 7: a faithful ρ, rational-representation-unipotent-point over L with i: V→U_r, then geometric-unipotence-unitriangular-embedding (U smooth) gives an embedding over k. Step 8 is elementary assembly. Edge cases: 1, G_a, G_m, the norm-one torus over R (not split), W_2 in char p; μ_p and α_p are excluded by smoothness, ℤ/p by geometric connectedness. No duplicate: perfect-solvable-unipotent-torus and commutative-multiplicative-part give no product splitting. No cycle.
